outcomes: A run that may publish knows its bound commit's ancestry and holds its publish credential before any repository code runs
A bound request without invocation.publication only gates: it plans no publication and starts no publication provider
A run whose credential provider negotiates publication-v1 resolves, opens, uploads and releases through that one session, and no repository process holds a publish credential
nonGoals: Uploading a member of an ecosystem other than npm, Go modules and OCI images under publication-v1; such a plan is refused before it opens
Publishing a bound request through publication-v1; its expected plan names no open or upload node, so the executing engine refuses the plan it builds

requirements.text: A run naming publish or deploy, or a bound request with invocation.publication, reads the ancestry of its bound commit (PUTNAMI_SOURCE_REVISION, else HEAD) at process start, before the bootstrap, an install or a hook, ignoring replace refs, grafts and the commit-graph; the run reuses it. It names a shallow clone and holds an error above 1,000,000 commits. Other runs read none. With publish enabled, the credential provider starts before the first hook, locally as on a hosted run.

A bound request without invocation.publication enables no publish purpose, even when its invocation.providers names publish, and says so on stderr. When its plan holds a task of a publication command or with declared registry or cloud effects, or its versions start a release-set publication, the executing engine refuses it before any release-set or deploy provider starts. A gate-only request plans no publish job and starts no release-set provider.

The engine uses publication-v1 only when the provider echoes it; otherwise nothing changes. With it, the provider resolves channels, one open sends plan, heads and ancestry after the barrier, and release sends artifacts, heads, ancestry and evidence. The provider refuses a second plan and a non-ancestor head. Open and release retry once after a timeout on a live session; release is idempotent by plan digest. A refusal names its code and moves no channel. Local and hosted runs open one plan.

Under publication-v1 a publication job gets a private 0700 outbox and no credential, credential descriptor or registry route. An engine upload node re-hashes the outbox, refuses a member, version or project the plan does not assign, asks the publish credential of the member's registry and uploads the npm tarball, Go zip or OCI layout itself, with published-image.json and one published-member event per upload. No descriptor means nothing packed. A reused publication job packed nothing; the release refuses.
